title: WWTP — overview
description: The plant at a glance: four numbers first, then the trends. Generated from contracts/tags.yaml; the band on each panel is the contract's `normal_low`/`normal_high`, which is a *specification* and not an alarm threshold — see docs/ALARM-TUNING.md.

panels.title: Influent flow
panels.description: How much is arriving, right now. The first question on a shift: more than design and the hydraulics are in trouble, less and something upstream has stopped.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeTo()::timestamptz AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'INFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW'   AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours' -- flow_m3h, latest -- one column: a stat panel draws one per numeric field

panels.title: Effluent flow
panels.description: Compare it with influent. **Effluent above influent means water is being added** — a dilution step, storm runoff, or a leak in the wrong direction.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeTo()::timestamptz AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'EFFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW'   AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours' -- flow_m3h, latest -- one column: a stat panel draws one per numeric field

panels.title: Aeration DO
panels.description: Dissolved oxygen in the aeration basin. **In range is not the same as true** — see the drift panel below, which is the one that catches a lying instrument.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeTo()::timestamptz AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:DO'   AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours' -- do_mg_l, latest -- one column: a stat panel draws one per numeric field

panels.title: Aeration air flow
panels.description:
What the control loop is actually commanding — the output, not the result. **This was effluent ammonia, and it was the wrong tile.** Ammonia moves by less than its 0.1 mg/L deadband over six hours, so the gateway stores almost nothing and this panel showed *No data* beside three live numbers, which reads as a failed instrument rather than a quiet one. Air flow is the output an operator's setpoint *moves*, so it is the one worth a tile — and it is the signal to watch when you change the setpoint.

The ammonia is not lost: its **compliance** figure is a 30-day mean and is on the permit dashboard, and its trend is on *Effluent quality* below. A number that only changes twice a week does not belong in a row read in five seconds.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeTo()::timestamptz AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:AIR_FLOW'   AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours' -- air_flow_m3h, latest -- one column: a stat panel draws one per numeric field

panels.title: Influent and effluent flow
panels.description: Two different quantities on one axis is wrong, and they are here anyway because the *shape* comparison is the point: effluent above influent means water is being added. The unit is the shared one.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'INFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- flow_m3h, raw tier

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'EFFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- flow_m3h, raw tier

panels.title: Dissolved oxygen
panels.description: Aeration basin DO. The band is the contract's 1.5-3.0 mg/L.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:DO'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- do_mg_l, raw tier

panels.title: Blower speed and air flow
panels.description: Two quantities, two units, **no band**. A threshold in rev/min drawn on a panel whose other series is m3/h is a number with no meaning, and a reader cannot tell which series it belongs to. When two units have to share a panel, the band is the thing that has to go, and the panel says so rather than implying the units agree.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:BLOWER_RPM'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- blower_rpm, raw tier

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:AIR_FLOW'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- air_flow_m3h, raw tier

panels.title: DO against air flow — is the probe telling the truth?
panels.description:
**The instrument-versus-process panel.** Normally these two move together: more air, more oxygen, higher DO. When the blower is working hard and DO sits low, the plant is being under-aerated. When the blower is working hard and DO sits comfortably high, *the probe is reading high and the process is not being aerated* — a drifting sensor, which no threshold on the DO reading can ever catch, because the reading never leaves its range.

This is the `do_sensor_drift` fault, and it is why this panel exists rather than a threshold. Two units on one axis and **no band**, for the same reason the blower panel has none: a mg/L threshold drawn here would be silently read as a limit on m3/h. Read the *divergence between the shapes*, not either axis.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:DO'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- do_mg_l, raw tier

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'AERATION:AHU-1:AIR_FLOW'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- air_flow_m3h, raw tier

panels.title: Effluent quality
panels.description: Ammonia and suspended solids, hourly tier, so a week on screen is 168 points rather than 12 000.

targets.rawSql: SELECT bucket AS time, mean AS value FROM reading_1h WHERE signal_id = 'EFFLUENT:FLOW:NH4'   AND bucket >= $__timeFrom() AND bucket <= $__timeTo() ORDER BY time -- nh4_mg_l, hourly tier
SELECT bucket AS time, mean AS value FROM reading_1h WHERE signal_id = 'EFFLUENT:FLOW:TSS'   AND bucket >= $__timeFrom() AND bucket <= $__timeTo() ORDER BY time -- tss_mg_l, hourly tier

panels.title: Sludge and digester
panels.description: Secondary clarifier blanket depth and digester pH. No band: metres and pH are not comparable, and a blanket depth band drawn on this panel would silently be read as a pH limit. Each needs its own panel to have a band, which is a layout decision this generator makes by refusing to draw one here.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'SECONDARY:SEC-CL-1:BLANKET'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- blanket_m, raw tier

SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '5 seconds', ts) AS time,        (array_agg(value ORDER BY ts DESC))[1] AS value,        max(quality) AS quality,        count(*) AS samples FROM reading WHERE signal_id = 'SLUDGE:DIG-1:PH'   AND ts >= $__timeFrom() AND ts <= $__timeTo() GROUP BY time ORDER BY time -- ph, raw tier

panels.title: How old is the reading behind each number?
panels.description:
**A stat panel cannot show you this, and the gap matters.** The four numbers above are the most recent *stored* reading, and the historian only stores one when it exceeds the signal's deadband — so a tile can be hours old while the instrument is perfectly healthy. Only seven of the fifty-seven signals have stored anything in the last hour, and the gateway reports filtering **94 %** of readings, which is exactly what a deadband is for.

This table is the difference between *the probe has failed* and *the ammonia moved less than 0.1 mg/L*. Same symptom, completely different action. Read it before you read a big number as a live one — and read *What has stopped reporting* below for the harder case, which is a signal with no recent reading at all.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT wanted.signal_id AS signal,
       wanted.field,
       now() - max(r.ts) AS age,
       count(r.ts) AS rows_stored_24h
FROM (VALUES ('INFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW', 'flow_m3h'), ('EFFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW', 'flow_m3h'), ('AERATION:AHU-1:DO', 'do_mg_l'), ('AERATION:AHU-1:AIR_FLOW', 'air_flow_m3h')) AS wanted(signal_id, field)
LEFT JOIN reading r
       ON r.signal_id = wanted.signal_id
      AND r.ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
WHERE wanted.signal_id IN ('INFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW', 'EFFLUENT:FLOW:FLOW', 'AERATION:AHU-1:DO', 'AERATION:AHU-1:AIR_FLOW')
GROUP BY wanted.signal_id, wanted.field
ORDER BY max(r.ts) NULLS FIRST

panels.title: What has stopped reporting
panels.description:
**The deadband's honest limit, shown rather than hidden.** A row exists when the value *moved*, so a signal whose value never moves produces one row and then nothing. Thirteen of the 57 signals do exactly that in a seeded week, and on a trend panel that looks like an outage and is not one. This table is why a panel that simply stops drawing is not evidence that a signal has failed — see sql/02-intermediate/02-04_gaps.md.

**Equipment state is not here and cannot be.** The `equipment` table carries no state column by design — a row that changes every scan is write amplification wearing a metadata costume — and no run-state signal exists in the contract, so "which pump is running" has no data to be a panel about. Run state is on the Modbus coils and the OPC UA address space. Building this panel means deciding how to get 21 equipment states into the historian at 50 Hz, which is an architecture decision rather than a panel.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT s.id AS signal,
       s.area,
       s.unit,
       max(r.ts) AS last_reading,
       now() - max(r.ts) AS silence
FROM signal s
LEFT JOIN reading r ON r.signal_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.id, s.area, s.unit
HAVING max(r.ts) IS NULL
    OR now() - max(r.ts) > interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY silence DESC NULLS FIRST
LIMIT 30
